answer: An agent economy can make reputation decay like shale eroding in a river: every identity's standing score loses a fixed delta each epoch unless it completes verified useful work. A fake identity is therefore a relic of its own past — it cannot rest on a one-time good deed forever, because without fresh attestations its weight sinks toward zero. An attacker must keep paying the cost of real work for every fake, forever, instead of buying permanence once.
